The game's first instruction, where the loader's stub at $081B jumps. Resets the stack, clears page 3, copies the KERNAL's 32-byte vector table ($FD30, the KERNAL is still switched in) to $0314, points the character-output vector at an RTS, makes the processor port's two low bits outputs, and with all RAM switched in ($01 = $14) copies the game state $CA00-$CFFF to $D000-$D5FF under the I/O chips, the copy a new game is restored from. Then, with I/O back ($01 = $35): copies $1000-$13FF to colour RAM, fills the text screen $0400-$07FF with spaces, blacks the border and background, clears the clock's bitmap cells $28F8-$291F and colours two strips of colour RAM. Falls into the restart at $40A3. Its bytes also serve $4AD7's screen shake as a table of random scroll values.

The restart entry, also where RUN/STOP with RESTORE returns through $42D6. Masks both CIAs' interrupts and clears them, sets $68B0 = 1, $42C1 = 0 and the music driver's request byte $1600 = 7, sets the keyboard port directions, VIC bank 0, matrix at $0C00 and bitmap at $2000 ($D018 = $38), multicolour bitmap mode, the five sprites (0 the cursor, 1-4 the doubled view-screen canvas at $0900-$09FF), starts the welcome message ($7E24) through $647B, installs the raster interrupt at $549B and the NMI at $427D, picks up the team list pointer $CA08 into $45/$46, waits for raster $80 and starts the raster interrupt at line $F8. Then the control menu ($41BD): shows portrait 6 on the right-hand monitor, closes the iris if it is open, clears the panels, draws screen 6 (the four control choices), and waits for F1, F3, F5 or F7; when the music driver's byte $1600 reads $82 first, the demonstration starts instead.
Read the keyboard's row lines with every column driven low ($DC00 = 0): F1 gives $EF, F3 $DF, F5 $BF, F7 $F7, and so does any other key on the same row line, Z or space for F1, for example.

The NMI handler (RESTORE). Masks CIA 2's interrupts, then tests the keyboard's row line 7, where RUN/STOP is: if it is low, resets the stack and returns into the restart at $40A3 (the address in $42D6/$42D7, pushed under a copy of the flags for the RTI); if not, returns to where it was.

Bytes no code reaches: three fragments that read as raster-interrupt stubs (INC $D02B, INC $D020 with an acknowledge, INC $D02A), each ending in JMP $FFFF with a word after it. A leftover from development.
Five zero bytes nothing reads.
Set to 0 at the restart; nothing reads it.
Unused: the byte after $42C1 that nothing reads or writes.
Pointer to the welcome message at $7E24, printed at the restart.
The welcome message pointer's high byte.
Unused: the byte between the welcome pointer and the input handlers that nothing reads or writes.

The four input handlers, chosen on the control menu by F1-F7: keyboard $5630, digital joystick $562C, analog joystick (paddles) $5526, light pen $54F1. The interrupt calls the chosen one every frame through the JMP at $54EE.

The row-line values of F1 ($EF), F3 ($DF), F5 ($BF) and F7 ($F7). The scan at $420C starts at X = 4 and so also tests the byte after, $42D2, the NMI pointer's low byte $7D: two keys held together on row lines 1 and 7 (left SHIFT and W, say) would match it and take the input handler from $42CE/$42CF, $DFEF.
The NMI handler's address, $427D.
The NMI pointer's high byte.

Draws a picture at cell column X, row Y. The picture at ($31) starts with its width in cells and height in cell rows, then the bitmap, row by row (width x 8 bytes for each cell row, written $140 apart), then the colours, packed three bytes to two cells: cell A takes byte 0 as its screen colours and byte 1's low nibble as its colour RAM; cell B takes (byte 1 >> 4) | (byte 2 << 4) as screen colours and byte 2's high nibble as colour RAM. Every icon, panel and portrait goes through it. Y swaps with $7D through $486B, so one register indexes both the source and the screen. Entered at $4324 with $4A1E set, it draws only the colours and leaves the registers on the stack.
The colour pass, also entered from $4922 to colour a portrait whose bitmap is already drawn.

Draws the selection frame around the icon at cell X, Y whose size is in $49F1/$49F2: a rectangle of multicolour pixels through $456A, one or (when $543F bit 1 is set) three pixels further out, drawn twice in colour $45D4 = 3 and so on down to 0, which leaves it erased, so the frame flashes. Returns early when $543F is 0, leaving the frame drawn.

Draws a rounded panel border at cell X-1, Y-1, $49F1 cells wide and $49F2 high: the four corner glyphs from $4A40 ORed into the bitmap, the top and bottom edges as $55 pairs, the sides as $01 and $40 columns. Called for each box listed after a screen's icons.
ORs the 8-byte corner glyph ending at $4A40+X into the cell at ($2B).
Draws a horizontal edge: $55 in two rows (from $7B) of each of $49F1 cells.
Draws a vertical edge: ORs $7B into all 8 rows of each of $49F2 cells, one cell row down each time.
Moves the bitmap pointer $2B one cell right (8 bytes).
Moves the bitmap pointer $2B one cell row down ($140 bytes).

Sets (carry set) or clears (carry clear) one pixel of the view-screen canvas, the four sprites at $0900-$09FF shown as one 48 x 42 picture: X is the column (0-47), Y the row (0-41). X from 24 moves to the right-hand sprite ($40 on), Y from 21 to the lower pair ($80 on); the byte is row x 3 + column / 8 and the bit comes from $49F4 or $49FC.

With carry clear, sets the multicolour pixel at X (0-159), Y (0-199) of the bitmap to the colour $45D4 (0-3) through the masks at $45DA and $45DE; with carry set, reads it, returning its colour (0-3) in A. Rows come from the tables at $1504/$151D.
The colour (0-3) $456A plots in.
Pixel row within the cell, kept by $456A.
The four colours as full bytes ($00, $55, $AA, $FF), masked to the pixel by $45DE.
Masks that keep everything but pixel 0-3 of a byte.
Masks that select pixel 0-3 of a byte.

Opens the iris on the view screen: clears circles of radius 0 to $12 out of the grey sprite canvas through $4698, so that the map drawn in the bitmap behind it shows through a growing round hole, with the step count and shift growing at radius 8 and $11 so the larger circles have no gaps; then sets $6C8C = 1 (the iris is open).
For iris_open: one more halving of each step ($4729) and twice as many steps ($4728), so that the bigger circles have no gaps. iris_close undoes it through iris_coarser.
Closes the iris: sets the canvas's pixels again in circles from radius $13 down to 1 ($4A0E = 1), the reverse of $45E2, and sets $6C8C = 0.
For iris_close: one halving fewer for each step ($4729) and half as many steps ($4728), the reverse of iris_finer.

Clears (or with $4A0E set, sets) the canvas pixels on a circle of radius X around the canvas centre (24, 21), by the shift-and-add rotation on the 8.8 coordinates at $FB-$FE: x -= y >> k, then y += x >> k (s_46ED returns the shift negated), for $4728 steps, with k in $4729. Y is the fraction the across coordinate starts with: 0, or $80 for a circle half a pixel further out, and the iris routines alternate the two.

Returns, in $F7/$F8, minus the 16-bit value there shifted right by $4729, rounded toward zero: a positive value is shifted and then negated ($470D), a negative one negated, shifted and left positive. $0500 shifted by 3 gives $FF60.
Negates the 16-bit value $F7/$F8.
The radius being drawn.
The fraction each circle's across coordinate starts with, $00 or $80 in turn ($4613), so that every other circle is half a pixel larger.
Steps left in the circle.
Set while $46ED is shifting a negative value.
Steps in one circle: $33, doubled at radius 8 and $11.
The rotation's shift: 3, one more at radius 8 and $11.
An RTS no code reaches.

Prints the string at ($3D) at cell column X, row $7D, six-line glyphs from the font at $1400 (address $1400 + code x 6 through $4873). Codes: 0-$37 a glyph, $38 the end of the string, $39 a new line, $80 and up a word from the word list (the pointer at $81B1 + 2 x (code - $80)), which is printed in place and can itself hold words.
Clears the lower half of the screen, cell rows 13-24: zeroes the bitmap rows and sets the screen colours to $4A62 and colour RAM to 5 (green).

Sets the screen pointers for cell column X, row Y: the bitmap byte in $2B/$2C (from the row tables at $1504/$151D, plus X x 8), the colour matrix byte in $2D/$2E ($0C00 + 40 Y + X) and the colour RAM byte in $2F/$30 ($D800 + 40 Y + X).
Multiplies A by Y, eight bits by eight: the 16-bit product in A (low) and Y (high).
Exchanges Y with $7D, keeping A. The drawing routines use it to run a source and a destination index in one register.
Points $3B/$3C at the glyph for code $4A0F: the font base $4A1F/$4A20 ($1400) plus six times the code.

Colours character A's status icon in the command panel, a block of 2 x 2 cells, with Y in both the colour matrix and colour RAM. The block's address low byte comes from $4A04 + A and is written into the operands of the two STAs below (the code rewrites itself); the four cell offsets come from $4A0A-$4A0D.
The low byte of the colour matrix STA's address, written from $4A04 for the character's icon.
The low byte of the colour RAM STA's address, written from $4A04 as well.

Puts the portrait of character $5436 on the right-hand monitor (cell column 28, row 2, 10 x 8 cells): blanks the area, clearing each cell's top line and rolling it down through $49A3; then, in seven passes, copies one pixel line of all 80 cells, line 7 first and line 1 last, into the top line of each cell and rolls the rows down a line, so the picture rolls on like a television; then colours it from the colour pointer through $4324. Line 0 of each cell is never copied: the monitor repeats line 1 there (live).
Moves eight rows of the monitor down one bitmap line at a time, from line $7B down to $4A1C, after waiting for raster line $64: the picture rolls on like a television.
Which half of a three-byte colour pair the picture drawer is on.
Width of the picture or box being drawn, in bytes (cells x 8 while drawing) or cells.
Height of the picture or box, in cell rows.
The eight single-bit masks, left pixel first, for the canvas.
The eight masks that clear one bit.

The low byte of each character's status icon in the colour matrix ($0C29, $0CA1, $0C2C, $0CA4, $0C2F, $0CA7): the six icons in two rows of three at the panel's top left, columns 1, 4 and 7 of cell rows 1 and 4.
The sixth character's icon cell ($A7). $4897's loop reads its cell offsets as $4A09 + X with X from 4 down to 1, so the offsets are the four bytes after it.
The four cells of a status icon, read last first: +$29, +$28, +1, +0.
0 while the iris opens, clearing canvas pixels; 1 while it closes, setting them again.
The code of the glyph being printed.
Cleared by $45E2; nothing reads it.
Set to $14 by $45E2; nothing reads it.
Frame width in pixels.
Frame height in pixels.

Frame top edge, in pixels.
How many words deep the printer is.
Roll start line.
Roll end line.
Line counter for the portrait roll.
Set while $42D9 is entered at $4324 for colours alone.
The font's base, $1400.
The font pointer's high byte.
Two pointers per portrait, its bitmap (10 x 8 cells, 640 bytes) and its packed colours (120 bytes), for portraits 0-7 (6 and 7 the same picture). $4A22 is the same table read one byte on.
The portrait table read one byte on, for the high byte of each pointer.
The portrait table's last byte ($F3, the high byte of $F315). The border code reads $4A40 + X with X from 1, so the corner glyphs start after it.
The four corner glyphs of a panel border, 8 bytes each ($4A41, $4A49, $4A51, $4A59), each read backwards from its last byte.
Set to 1 while the transporter routines close and open the iris again, then 0; nothing reads it.

Draws screen A (0-8, from the table at $789C) and makes it current ($5435): for each icon record (11 bytes: picture pointer, cell column and row, flags, text pointer, text column and row, handler) draws the picture through $42D9 and prints its text through $472B, until a record starting $FFFF; then draws each panel border listed after it (4 bytes: width, height, column, row, up to another $FFFF) through $446C. Leaves $543F = 3, or 0 when the screen has no borders.

Zoff V explodes: with the sprites off, for 256 frames sets the vertical and horizontal fine scroll from the bytes of the code at $4000 and $5000 (any byte, used as a random number) and flashes the border and background through the 16 colours at $5489, then puts the scroll back and falls into $4B35.

Ends what is on screen and goes to the start menu: closes the iris if it is open and shows portrait 6, sets $CF7F, clears the leave request $6932, drops the saved icon pointer if a two-step choice was under way, and jumps to $74B9.

The command loop every screen runs: clears $68B2 and the icon group $543E, then (at $4B6C) checks each frame for a reason to leave and, if none, tests the cursor against the current screen's icons. Leaves for the start menu when $6932 asks or the mission is over ($CA05 = 0, or $1F with every objective met), shakes the screen when Zoff V has been destroyed without being captured ($CA05 bits 2-3 = %01), returns to the team screen when the character on show is no longer able to act, and redraws the team screen when a character has died ($68B2). Then $4BC4 tests the icons in turn.
The loop's entry for callers that wait for an icon inside a two-step choice ($4C9C, $7378, $7418): the same tests as $4B64 without clearing the group.
A door has just been opened ($CF82, set by the lock-picking in the interrupt): with the view screen open, redraw the door icons through $5417, then clear the flag.

Tests the icon at ($37) against the cursor cell ($76 row, $77 column). It is skipped unless flag bit 0 (enabled) is set. An icon without flag bit 1 must also carry every bit of the mask at $545F for the choice under way ($543E): $05 when there is none, so a plain icon needs bit 2 as well as bit 0. An icon with flag bit 1 can be chosen only when no choice is under way. Inside the icon's rectangle, draws the flashing frame through $43B4 and waits; fire (cleared $78) selects it. A selected icon that has a text label writes $DE to the sound driver's byte $1601. An icon with flag bit 1 starts a two-step choice: its flags' bits 2-7 become the group, the frame stays, and the loop runs again for the second icon (an object, a character, a direction), whose handler records the choice and returns; the first icon's handler then runs, unless $5439 cancels. Any other icon's handler runs at once through the JMP at $4CDC, whose operand is written here.
The operand of the JMP at $4CDC, the chosen icon's handler: low byte.
The chosen icon's handler: high byte.
Next icon: $53D7 steps $37 on; at the list's end the loop starts again.
Points $37/$38 at the first icon record of the current screen $5435, through the table at $789C.

Fills the left-hand column of the objects screen (screen 4, icon records from $5482) with the objects lying in the current location $5437, from the 7-byte object records at ($CD96), skipping the first $5440 of them for paging. Each icon gets the object's picture and the flag bits that let a command choose it: bit 3 (Pick-up) when object flag 3 is clear and the object weighs less than 255 minus the weight the character carries (entity byte 7), bit 5 (Ready for use) when object flag 1 is set, bit 6 (Activate) when object flag 2 is set, each with bit 0 (enabled). Objects 0-2, the two transporter beacons and the transporter, get no flags unless the character is 2, Manto. $544F records which object each icon shows. Eight icons hold objects; the ninth is the page arrow ($5480, flags $FD) when more objects follow or a later page is showing, and a blank otherwise. A skip that runs past the last object starts again at the first.

The same for the middle column (five icons from $5484, a sixth for the page arrow): the objects carried by character $5436 (object flag 0 set, byte 1 the carrier), skipping $5441 of them. Each gets bit 4 (Drop), bit 5 (Ready for use) when object flag 1 is set, and bit 6 (Activate) when object flag 2 is set and it is not object 0 or 1, the beacons. $5449 records them. First puts the picture of the object held ready (entity byte 8, 0 for none) into the icon record at $7A44, below the Ready icon.

Fills the battle screen's location scan (screen 5, icon records from $7E22) with the entities standing in location $5446 that are alive (entity flag 1 clear), starting $5442 records into the entity table: each icon shows the entity's figure from the table at $6CFE. $5457 records which entity is in each, $FF for an empty icon. Eight icons hold entities; the ninth is the page arrow when the list was full, or a blank.

Not a table: shake_screen reads the bytes from here (LDA $5000,X at $4AFF) as random numbers, and this address is the last byte of the STA at $4FFE. The rest of list_people_here: walks the entity records from the page start, putting each living entity standing in $5446 into the next icon, until eight are shown or the fiftieth record is passed; blank icons fill the rest.

For the transporter: fills the objects screen's left column with the entities standing in beacon 1's location (object 0's byte 1, $CD99), their figures and flags $81 (group bit 7, for choosing whom to beam), skipping $5444 of them. If the beacon is being carried ($CD98 bit 0) sets $5488 and leaves the icons blank. $544F records the entities.
The same for the middle column (five icons) and beacon 2 (object 1, its location $CDA0), with $5445 for paging, $5449 for the record of entities, and $5488 if that beacon is carried.
Clears the flags of the eight left-hand and five middle icons of the objects screen, so that none can be chosen (used when a transporter beacon is carried).
Puts the three destinations of Manto's ballistic control into the objects screen's left-hand icons, from the table at $5465 (picture pointer and flags for each icon) until the icon list's end.
Unused: nothing calls it except $717F, which nothing reaches. Fills the battle screen's icons from the character's route list (entity bytes 10-16) with each step's figure from $6CFE.
Steps $2D/$2E to the next 7-byte object record and counts it in $5438; returns carry set at the list's $FFFF end.
Steps $2D/$2E to the next 18-byte entity record and counts it in $5447; returns carry set after the fiftieth.
Steps $37/$38 to the next 11-byte icon record; returns carry set when it reaches the $FFFF that ends the list.
Converts the cursor sprite's position into a cell: row ($D001 - $20) / 8 into $76, column ((X with its ninth bit) / 2 - 2) / 4 into $77, in multicolour cells.
After a lock has been picked ($CF82): every direction icon of screen 2 whose flags have bit 3 set (an exit shown locked) gets flags 5, so it can be chosen, and its twin on screen 5 flags $39.
The current screen, 0-8.
The character on show, 0-5 (6 when none).
The location of the character on show.
The slot (object, entity or direction) the second step of a two-step choice picked.
Set by a handler to cancel the two-step choice under way.
Set by a handler (a page arrow) to keep the second step going.
The first icon's width, kept while the second is chosen.
The first icon's height, kept while the second is chosen.
Unused: the byte after the first icon's kept height that nothing reads or writes.
The group of the two-step choice under way, 0 when none.
How $43B4 draws the frame: 0 drawn and left, 1 flashed once, 3 the large frame.
How many objects in the location the list skips, for paging.
How many carried objects the list skips.
How many entity records the location scan skips, for paging.
Counts the records the list routines pass; nothing reads it.
Paging for the first transporter list.
Paging for the second transporter list.
The location the battle screen's scan shows.
The entity the list routines are on.
The icon the list routines are filling.
Which object each of the five carried icons shows.
Which object (or, for the transporter, which entity) each of the eight left-hand icons shows.
Which entity each of the eight scan icons shows, $FF for none.

The flag bits an icon needs, by the two-step choice under way ($543E): $05 (bits 0 and 2) when none, then $09, $11, $21, $41 and $81 for groups 1 to 5. Six bytes; the interrupt's search of the eight scan slots at $5457 reads one byte too far, into the first of them ($5ADC).

The left-hand icons of the ballistic control, 3 bytes each (picture pointer, icon flags): the three destination pictures $FB18, $FBB4 and $FB66 (flags $81) in the second, fifth and eighth icons, the blank picture $8D34 in the rest.
The picture of the "more" arrow, $E88C.
The more arrow pointer's high byte.
The objects screen's first left-hand icon record, $7AB2.
The left-hand icons pointer's high byte.
Its first middle icon record, $7A70.
The middle icons pointer's high byte.
255 minus the weight the character carries, while the objects are listed.
Unused: the byte after weight_left that nothing reads or writes.
Set when a transporter beacon is being carried, so its list is blank.
The 16 colours the explosion flashes.
The raster interrupt's address, $549B.
The interrupt pointer's high byte.

The raster interrupt, line $F8, every frame. Saves the registers and every zero-page and drawing variable the main program uses, so that it can draw on the screen itself, then jumps to the chosen input handler (operand written at $54EE), which moves the cursor and ends at $5754 for the game's own frame.
The input handler's jump; its operand is set from $42C6 or $42D4.

The operand of the JMP at $54EE, low byte: the input handler. It is the one chosen on the control menu, written from input_handlers at $425F, or input_demo ($5570), written at $4221 when the demonstration starts.
The input handler: high byte.
Light pen: the cursor follows the pen's latch ($D013, $D014), and any key clears $78 (fire).
Analog joystick (paddles): the cursor's row from paddle 1 ($D419), its column from paddle 2 ($D41A); the button on joystick line 1 clears $78.
Unused: nothing reaches it. Limits A to the cursor's rows $9A-$E6 and stores it as the cursor's Y.

The demonstration's input: any key ends the demonstration ($6932 = 1, the script restarts at entry $6C). Otherwise the cursor walks one pixel a frame towards the next point of the demo script at $1571 (X in $692E, Y in $692F); there it waits $78 frames with fire pressed ($6933), then takes the next point, every fourth point starting the "Shadowfire demonstration" message again. A point with Y = $FF would end the script ($6932), but none has one: the script ends by clicking Quit on the team screen and then on the start menu, which goes back to the control menu (live).

Digital joystick in port 1, read through $DC01 (entered with X = 1; the keyboard entry at $5630 uses X = 2). Each direction held moves the cursor faster, its speed ($68E1 across, $68E2 down) rising from 2 to 6 every 10 or 20 frames, and the cursor wraps from one edge of the panel area to the other. Fire clears $78.
Keyboard control: the same as the joystick with X = 2, so that the masks at $6825-$682D pick keyboard row lines instead of the joystick's bits.
Keeps the cursor inside rows $9A-$E6 and columns $18-$140, for the paddles and light pen.

The game's own part of the interrupt, every frame after the input handler. Plays a frame of music ($1606). While the game is not running ($68B0 set: the menus and the start) it skips the status bars, the entity's second of simulation and the clock's roll, and jumps to the ticker ($5FEF), which goes on as in play to the view map's cell, the entity's list of reachable locations and the step to the next entity; after the fiftieth entity it stops there. Otherwise, in order: grows or shrinks the status screen's bars one step, runs one entity's second of simulation (entity $66D1, record at ($45): one of the fifty each frame, so each one once a second), rolls the clock digits, scrolls the ticker, updates one cell of the view screen's map, rebuilds the entity's list of reachable locations, and after the fiftieth entity counts down the time lock, the self-destruct and the mission clock. Ends by restoring everything at $637E.

The status screen's five bars, one step each frame while $66CC says the screen shows them ($66CD set: only the two weight bars, on the objects screen). Bar 0 is strength, (+4) x the character's strength factor at $CF85 / 256; bar 1 agility, the average of the base at $CFB7 and +5; bar 2 stamina (+6); bar 3 the weight carried (+7), drawn red; bar 4 the weight again, or the strength figure when that is lower, drawn green over bar 3. A dead character's bars all fall to 0.

Bar X: half its value is the length it should have, $66BE,x the length it has. One step longer draws a column of its colour from $66C3; one step shorter draws colour 0, or bar 3's red where bar 4 retreats over it. Rows from $66AA/$66AF (upper) and $66B4/$66B9 (lower).
The time lock ($CF83 seconds left, set by the time delay unit): every entity but the one in $CF84 is frozen, its frame going straight to the view screen at $60CF.
One entity's second. A dead entity (status bit 1) does nothing.

Enemies $08-$25 that are neither fighting nor retreating look into every location they can reach (+10 onwards): any living team member there puts them into combat (status 8, defending). Entities $26-$31 never look; Kryxix and Zoff are handled at $5D93.

A team member's second. Colours the status icon from $68B7 by status (white idle, blue moving, black dead, yellow retreating, orange defending, purple attacking, green picking a lock), and sets the team screen icon's flag bit 0 (enabled), the icon records at $78AE, unless the character is moving or dead (status bits 0-1).
Strength below $80: on odd seconds the heartbeat sound ($1602 = $0F) and the status icon flashes grey ($BB), or black below $40.

Recovery. (255 - strength) x stamina / 256 is added to the strength fraction at $68FC: the weaker the character and the more stamina, the faster. It is halved while defending and quartered while attacking or retreating. Each time the fraction overflows, strength rises by 1 (to at most $FF), and every 32nd such point costs a point of stamina through the fraction at $CFC3.

Load against strength: the limit is strength x $CF85 / 256. Over it, agility (+5) falls each second by the excess / 16, its remainder taken from the fraction at $CFBD (the four low bits, gathered in reverse order by the LSR/ROL pairs), and not below 0.

Under the limit: with P = (limit - load) x stamina, agility (+5) rises each second by P / 4096 in whole points, to at most $FF, and bits 8-11 of P, reversed by the LSR/ROL pairs, go into the fraction at $CFBD (at most 15/256 of a point), which carries into agility when it overflows. Stamina is charged through $CFC3, as recovery charges it, in a second whose fraction bits are not all 0: the BEQ at $59D4 tests the last ROL, whether or not a whole point was gained.

Picking a lock (status $10): the door's counter at $CFC9 + $CF81 falls by 8 a second, from $FF, so about 32 seconds. When it passes 0 the door is open: the counter is set to 0, the character goes idle, $CF82 tells the command loop to redraw the doors, and "SEVRINA HAS OPENED THE DOOR" ($7F63) is queued, the name fixed in the text.
Moving (status bit 0). A team member pays a point of strength every fourth second of walking, through the fraction at $68FC, and dies when it reaches 0.

Anyone else whose destination is $A3, the Enigma Force's attack craft, has been beamed aboard and leaves play through $64CD: Kryxix queues "AMBASSADOR KRYXIX HAS BEEN RESCUED" and sets $CA05 bit 1, Zoff "ZOFF HAS BEEN CAPTURED" and bit 4.
The step countdown (+1) falls by 1 a second; at 0 the entity arrives: countdown 1, status 0 (idle).

With the battle screen's location scan on show ($8189), an entity arriving at the scanned location $5446 takes the first empty slot of the eight (its figure drawn in the icon), and one leaving it empties its slot (the blank picture $8D32).
Leaving the scanned location: find the entity's slot. The loop runs to nine, so it also tests $545F, the first icon-group mask, which holds 5: Torik, not on show, would overwrite that mask with $FF.

Arriving: the first slot holding $FF. When the slot found is the ninth ($545F, which only a $FF there could give), the page arrow is drawn after it; filling the eighth slot, the last real one, draws no arrow.
A team member's arrival at any of the six locations in $68EA runs that location's routine from $68F0, through the JSR at $5B91 whose operand is written here.
The operand of the JSR at $5B91, written from $68F0 before each call.
The high byte of the location routine's address, from $68F1.

Arrived: the location (+2) becomes the destination (+3). A team member who walks into Kryxix's location while he is alive and not yet following queues "<NAME> HAS LOCATED AMBASSADOR KRYXIX" (the name token at $8098); if it is Zark, also "AMBASSADOR KRYXIX FOLLOWS ZARK", and $CF80 = 1 from then on.
Combat, for an entity attacking ($0C), defending (8) or retreating (4-7); Kryxix and Zoff never fight. $68E0 keeps the status's combat bits.

The damage dealt: strength x $CF85 / 256. An enemy hits the six team members with it, the same in its own location and in each adjacent one. A team member hits entities 8-$31 with the weapon held ready (+8): $CF15 gives its strength, the high nibble meant for the same location and the low nibble for adjacent ones, $20 being bare hands. Each nibble x 16 x the damage / 256 goes into $68D7 (same location) and $68D8-$68DE (the seven adjacent), but only $68D7 is read ($5CB3): the high nibble decides the damage in every location in reach. Kryxix and Zoff (6 and 7) are on neither list, so nobody can harm them.

For each living target standing in one of the attacker's reachable locations (+10 onwards; the first is its own): the same-location damage ($68D7: X stays 0 through the loop) x 4, or x 8 when attacking into the attacker's own destination, comes off the target's strength (+4) and its fraction at $68FC. Strength below 0 kills it through $64CD.
A target that was idle, moving or picking a lock turns to defend (status 8); a team member hit so queues "<NAME> UNDER ATTACK", one of the six token messages from $8179.

After the round: a defender or retreater with nobody in range goes idle. An attacker with nobody left at its destination advances: defending if it is already there, otherwise moving on (status 1, or 5 while anyone is still in range). A moving entity takes the moving branch at $5A38 and does not fight until it arrives.

Everyone but the team, outside combat. An enemy with a team member in its own location turns to defend. Kryxix, once he follows ($CF80), walks to Zark's location whenever Zark is elsewhere (a step of 1 second).

Patrols, for an entity whose +7 has bit 7 set. +8 picks the patrol script from the table at $BDC0, +7 holds the position in it (bits 0-5) and the direction (bit 6 set: walking it backwards). A script is a length byte, then pairs of a time and a location.
Waits out the step countdown (+1) first.

Backwards: the next location is the one two bytes back, and the time is the current pair's time as it stands, where forwards it is multiplied by 4: a patrol walks back four times as fast as it came. At the start of the script, a chained patrol (+5 bit 7) moves to its next script through $5ED0, another turns round.

Forwards: the next pair, time x 4. At the end of the script, a chained patrol moves on through $5ED0; Zoff, at the end of his, has escaped: he leaves play through $64CD, "ZOFF HAS ESCAPED" is queued, six cells of the ship's map at $85CD-$85CF and $85ED-$85EF become $96, and $68B3 = 1, a flag nothing reads. Anyone else turns round.
Takes the step: +7 = the position and direction, the destination (+3) the pair's location, the step countdown (+1) its time, and status bit 0 (moving).

Chooses a chained patrol's next script. +6 (bits 0-6) picks the chain from the table at $BF54, +5 holds the position in it (bits 0-5) and its direction (bit 6). A chain is a length byte, then script numbers; bit 6 of a number reverses the script. The chain is walked forwards and backwards in turn. The new script number goes into +8, and +7 starts it at its beginning forwards ($80), or at its end backwards (its length - 2, with bits 6-7 set), as bit 6 of the entry and the chain's direction (XOR, in $682F) say.
The time lock holds everything else here.

The rolling clock: during the frames of entities 1-8, each digit cell moving to a new value scrolls down one pixel row and takes the new digit's next row from $6804/$680C/$6814/$681C, so the digit rolls in over eight frames. The seconds' units ($2918) always roll; $68B1 bits 0, 1 and 2 roll the seconds' tens ($2910), the minutes' units ($2900) and the minutes' tens ($28F8) when they change too.

The message ticker, every fourth frame: scrolls the strip at $2B48 two bits left ($63D7 twice). While a message runs, the looping voice-1 sound is $3E and the cell at $D91B flashes through the colours at $68A8; when it ends, the sound is $30 (unless the heartbeat $0F is on) and the cell goes black.

Every eighth shift, the next character: from the buffer at $66D8 ($66CF the position), or, at the end of a message, the next one queued at $67D8/$67E8 (read index $67F9, write index $67FA, sixteen entries). It is expanded into the buffer first: tokens of $80 and over are words from the table at $81B1, nested through the stack ($67F8 the depth), $39 becomes a space ($24), and $38 ends a message or a word. With nothing queued, spaces scroll.
The character's six glyph rows go into $67FB+2 to +7, for the scroll to shift in.

The view screen's map, while it is open ($6C8C): one of sixteen location cells a frame (entity numbers $00-$1F); the seventeenth of the tables, two right and two down, is never visited. In frames $10-$1F the cell's location ($6830) is searched for the next living entity after the last one shown ($6896), in turn round all fifty, and that entity's map icon (the first pointer of its four bytes at $6CFE) is drawn at the cell's column $6852 and row $6863. In frames $00-$0F a cell whose occupant changed is blanked ($8D08): so each icon flashes, and a location with several takes them in turn.
Rebuilds the entity's reachable locations (+10 to +17) through $65EA, then steps to the next entity; after the fiftieth, back to the first.
Once a second, after the fiftieth entity, when the game is running: the time lock counts down, and while it holds nothing else does.

The self-destruct, armed ($CA06): $CA07 counts down the seconds. At 0: the music stops, $CA05 bit 2 is set, "ZOFF V HAS BEEN DESTROYED" is queued, the kill count $CF67/$CF68 is set to 42, and the first eight entities (the team, Kryxix and Zoff) die through kill_entity unless they are aboard the attack craft ($A3) or dead already. kill_entity counts Kryxix and Zoff as they die, so the count ends at 44 when both were alive aboard Zoff V. Then bit 3 is cleared, so the ship counts as destroyed, not captured.
At 240, 180, 120 and 60 seconds ($68E6-$68E9): "4 MINUTES UNTIL DETONATION" (the digit written into the message at $80F2), down to "1 MINUTE UNTIL DETONATION".
The mission clock, minutes and seconds in four digits at $CA03, $CA02, $CA01 and $CA00. Counting down, $68B1 records which digits changed for the rolling display.

Past 00:00 the clock counts up from 00:01 ($CA04 = 1): Kryxix, unless already dead, is executed (status 2, "AMBASSADOR KRYXIX HAS BEEN EXECUTED"), and "WAR HAS BEEN DECLARED BY THE REPUBLIC" is queued.
Counting up; at 99:59 it stops at $6473.
The four digits' glyphs, upside down (row 7 first), into $6804, $680C, $6814 and $681C for the rolling display.
Puts back every variable the interrupt saved, acknowledges the raster interrupt and returns.
Shifts the ticker strip one bit left: for each glyph row 2-7, the next bit from $67FB+row goes into the right of twelve cells at $2B48+row, eight bytes apart. Counts the shift in $66D0.

Unused: nothing calls it. Returns carry set when location A lies inside the rectangle from ($6C92, $6C93) to ($6C94, $6C95), reading the location's coordinates through the tables at $B1E4 and, for locations $80 and over, $B248 rather than the $B2E4 the rest of the game uses. $6C94 and $6C95 are never written. Probably an earlier way of choosing what the view screen's map shows.

Unused: nothing calls it. Draws the picture at ($31) at the map cell of the location record at ($2D), two cells per step from column $0F and row 1 relative to the corner ($6C96, $6C97), except at the centre cell (column $13, row 5).
Y = X x 11, the offset of icon record X in a screen's list.

Counting up past 99:59: the minutes' tens digit has reached 10. Sets the clock counting down again ($CA04 = 0) and leaves the digits undrawn, so the next second shows 99:59 and the countdown starts over.

Queues the message at A (low) and Y (high) for the ticker: into $67D8/$67E8 at the write index $67FA, which wraps after 16. Nothing checks for a full queue: sixteen messages waiting at once would bring the write index round to the read index, and the queue would look empty.

Draws one step of bar X in colour A (0-3): at the bar's length $66BE,x, the pixel (length / 2) AND 3 of cell (length AND $F8) is set to the colour's bit pattern (pixel_keep, pixel_mask, colour_bits from plot_pixel), the same byte into all eight rows of the upper cell at ($2B) and the lower one at ($2D).

Entity $66D1, record at ($45), leaves play: killed, or beamed aboard the attack craft, or escaped. A team member's status icon goes black, the team screen icon becomes the picture at ($FF2E), or at ($8D82) for Manto and Maul, and is disabled; $68B2 = 1 redraws the team screen; "<NAME> HAS BEEN ELIMINATED" is queued (the name token in $7F65) unless Zoff V has been destroyed; the survivors' count $CF4C falls, and at 0 $CA05 bit 0 is cleared, which ends the mission.

Anyone else adds one to the count of enemies killed or captured, two decimal digits in $CF67 (tens) and $CF68 (units), so Kryxix rescued and Zoff captured or escaped count too. When the count reaches 44, $CA05 gets bits 2 and 3: Zoff V captured. Kryxix's execution ($62BB) sets his status without coming here, so after it kills alone reach only 43; the self-destruct sets the count to 42 before Kryxix and Zoff die.
Every object the entity carried (object flag bit 0 set, +1 its number) is dropped where it stands: +1 becomes the location and bit 0 is cleared. Then the entity's status becomes 2, dead.
Returns carry set when a living member of the team stands in location A.

Rebuilds +10 to +17 of the entity at ($45): +10 is its own location, then the destination of each exit of that location whose door is open or absent (the door number in bits 3-7 of the exit's second byte, open when $CFC9 holds 0 for it); $FF fills the rest. The exits come from the location record (through $B1E4, or $B2E4 for $80 and over): its third byte is a mask with a bit for each exit, then two bytes for each. Y swaps through $486B between the two records.
A team member has reached location $4E: Zoff (entity 7) starts his patrol, +7 bit 7.
Location $41: entities 11 to 18 start patrolling, +7 = $80 each.
Location $2E: entity 8 starts patrol script $16 from its beginning.
Location $4C: entity 8 starts patrol script $17.
Location $4F: entity 9 starts patrol script $18.
Location $2F: entity 9 starts patrol script $19.
An RTS nothing reaches, after trigger_9b's own.
The five status bars' upper cell rows: low bytes here, high bytes at $66AF ($31A0 strength, $3560 agility, $3920 stamina, $3CE0 twice for the two weight bars, which share a row).
High bytes of bar_rows.
The bars' lower cell rows, $140 below: low bytes here, high bytes at $66B9.
High bytes of bar_rows_lower. Its last byte, $66BD, is also read as bar_length - 1 when bar 4 asks for bar 3's length.
bar_rows_lower's last high byte. The bar code indexes bar_length from 1, so its STA $66BD,X (X = 5 down to 1) and CMP $66BD,X land on $66BE-$66C2, never here.
The length each of the five bars has on screen, in half-pixels.
Bar 3's length, the red weight bar.
Bar 4's length, the green weight bar.
The bars' colours: 3 for strength, agility, stamina and the green weight bar, 1 for the red.
The pixel within the cell for bar_step.
The colour for bar_step.
Bar 0's value, strength x $CF85 / 256: also the load limit.
Bar 1's value.
Set while the screen on show has the bars (the status screen, and the objects screen's weight bar).
Set on the objects screen: only bars 3 and 4 are drawn.
Unused: the byte between the bar flags and the ticker's position that nothing refers to.
The position in the ticker's buffer at $66D8.
Counts the ticker's one-bit shifts: a new character every eight, and the colour of the flashing light.
The entity whose second the interrupt is running, 0-49; also counts the frames of each second.
The glyph row ticker_shift is on.
The interrupt's general working byte (the main program uses it too).
A second working byte: the reachable-location index, and list_reachable's exit count.
Patrols: the position in the script, or the chain's direction bits.
Patrols: the direction bits, or the chain position.
The time of the patrol step being taken.
The message being shown, expanded: 256 bytes, $38 ending it.
The message queue, sixteen entries: low bytes of the messages' addresses.
The message queue's high bytes.
How many words deep the expansion is.
The queue's read index.
The queue's write index.
The next character's glyph rows (+2 to +7), shifted out one bit at a time.
The seconds' units digit when the time delay unit was activated: written, and read by nothing.
The rolling clock's incoming rows, eight bytes for each digit: seconds' units here, then $680C, $6814 and $681C. Rows 2-7 hold the new digit's glyph upside down.
The seconds' tens digit's incoming rows.
The minutes' units digit's incoming rows.
The minutes' tens digit's incoming rows.
Unused: the byte before the input masks that nothing refers to.

The bits the joystick and keyboard handlers test, two bytes for each test, the joystick's port bits then the keyboard's row lines: $6825 up or down ($03, $66), $6827 left or right ($0C, $90), $6829 down ($02, $24), $682B right ($08, $10), $682D fire ($10, $09).
Left or right: the joystick's bits $0C, the keyboard's row lines $90.
The direction bit of a patrol chain, for next_patrol.
The location in each of the view screen's map cells, $FF where there is none: seventeen bytes, the first sixteen filled by find_view_locations.
The entity each map cell showed last.
The map cells' cell columns on the screen: a star of the eight directions at distances 1 and 2 around column $13.
The map cells' cell rows, around row 5.
Each map cell's offset across from the character's location, -2 to +2.
Each map cell's offset down, -2 to +2.
The entity each map cell shows next, the search's starting point.
The colours of the ticker's flashing light, one per shift.
Set while the game is not being played (the start, the menus): the interrupt then only plays music and scrolls the ticker.
Which clock digits roll this second: bit 0 the seconds' tens, bit 1 the minutes' units, bit 2 the minutes' tens.
Set when a team member dies: the command loop redraws the team screen.
Set when Zoff escapes; nothing reads it.
Combat: how many targets the attacker had in reach this second.
Combat: how many of them stood at the attacker's destination.
Combat: the attacker's destination.
The status icon's colour for each status, 0-$1F: $11 idle, $66 moving, $00 dead, $77 retreating, $88 defending, $44 attacking, $55 picking a lock.

Combat: the damage for each of the attacker's eight reachable locations, the first its own: $68D7 the same-location damage, $68D8-$68DE the adjacent. Only $68D7 is read: the loop at $5CB3 reads it with X 0 for every location, so every target in reach takes the same-location damage, and a weapon's adjacent strength is never used.
Combat: the strength byte of the weapon used; written, and read by nothing.
Combat: the attacker's status AND $0C.
The cursor's speed across, 2 to 6, rising while a direction is held.
The cursor's speed down.
Frames a direction across has been held.
Frames a direction up or down has been held.
The cursor's X position in two-pixel steps: the sprite's X is twice it. The self-destruct's warnings index from here as well, X = 1 to 4, so their table is the four bytes after it.
The self-destruct's warnings, in seconds left: 60, 120, 180 and 240.
Six locations where a team member's every arrival runs a routine, from $68F0: $4E, $41, $2E, $4C, $4F and $2F.
The six routines for trigger_locations.
The trigger routines' table read one byte on, for the high bytes.
Each entity's strength fraction: walking takes $40 a second, recovery adds to it, and wounds come off it.
The demonstration's next cursor point, X.
The demonstration's next cursor point, Y.
Frames the demonstration waits at a point, with fire held.
The demonstration's position in its script at $1571, two bytes a point.
Set to leave for the start menu: by a key during the demonstration, or at its end.
Set while the demonstration holds fire at a point.

Prepares the movement screen (2) and the battle screen (5) for location A: points $3F at its record and reads its map coordinates into $6C90/$6C91. For each of the eight directions, from bit 7 of the exits mask: a direction with no exit gets the empty arrow pictures ($6CAE for screen 2, $6CCE for screen 5), no flags and the handler at $7601; one with an exit gets the filled arrows ($6C9E, $6CBE), flags $3D on screen 2 and $39 on screen 5 ($08 on both when the exit's door is locked: shown, not selectable), and the next of the eight direction handlers ($6CDE, $6CEE), so handler n always means the location's nth exit. Points the movement screen's description text at the record after the exits, and draws the map through $6A50 unless $6DC6 is set.

Draws the view screen's map around map position X, Y. $FF, $FF (a place off the map) draws two pictures instead, from $6DC7 and $6DC9. Otherwise a window of 5 x 5 tiles from (X - 1, Y - 1), each tile 2 x 2 cells: its number from the 32 x 32 tile map at ($84C7), its colour from the map at ($84C9), its four characters from the tile set at ($BF94), their bitmaps from ($C286). Rows and columns outside the map are tile $31. Colour RAM is filled with $0E first. Then finds the locations to show through $6BB7.
Colour RAM under the map, 10 rows of 10 cells from $D837, set to $0E.
One row of tiles: their four characters into $6C64 (top) and $6C6E (bottom), the tile's colour into all four of its cells at $6C78.
The row's two character rows into the bitmap from $21B8, eight bytes each, the colours into the screen matrix from $0C36; stops when the bitmap reaches $2E38, ten character rows down.

For sixteen of the map's seventeen cells (X = 15 down to 0; the last, two right and two down, is left out), looks for a location at the character's coordinates plus the cell's offset ($6874, $6885), searching all $A4 locations, and stores it in $6830, or $FF.
Steps the map's bitmap pointer ($2B) and colour pointer ($2D) down one cell row.
Shifts the word at $F7/$F8 left X times: x 32 for a map row, x 4 for a tile, x 8 for a character.
A tile row outside the map: blank characters.
Unused: nothing calls it. Splits A into its low nibble, kept in $6C9A, and its high nibble, returned in A.
The tile row's characters: ten for the upper character row, then ten at $6C6E for the lower.
The lower character row of the tile row.
The tile row's colours, the same for the four cells of each tile: twenty bytes, the upper row then the lower.
The same table one byte on, for the tile's right-hand cell.
The colours of the lower character row.
The lower row's right-hand cells.
Set while the view screen's iris is open, showing the map.
The exits mask being shifted, a direction a bit.
How many exits build_directions has met.
The location's map column, then the window's left column.
The location's map row, then the row being drawn.
The window's left column, kept.
The window's top row, kept.
Unused_in_window's right edge, never written.
Unused_in_window's bottom edge, never written.
Unused_place_icon's corner, never written.
Unused_place_icon's corner row, never written.
Unused_nibbles' low nibble.
The location find_view_locations is testing.
The coordinates find_view_locations looks for: across.
And down.
The movement screen's filled arrow pictures, one for each of the eight directions.
The movement screen's filled arrows, read one byte on.
The movement screen's empty arrows.
The movement screen's empty arrows, one byte on.
The battle screen's filled arrows.
The battle screen's filled arrows, one byte on.
The battle screen's empty arrows.
The battle screen's empty arrows, one byte on.
The movement screen's eight exit handlers, $6E47 to $6E63, given in order to a location's exits.
The battle screen's eight exit handlers, $7144 to $7160.
Four bytes for each of the fifty entities: its icon on the view screen's map, then its figure for the battle screen's scan and the team lists.
The same table one byte on.
The figure pointers, entity_pictures + 2.
The same, one byte on.
Set while build_directions must leave the map alone (the door routines rebuilding the arrows).
The two pictures for a place off the map: the upper one here, the lower at $6DC9.
The upper off-map picture's high byte.
The lower off-map picture.
The lower off-map picture's high byte.

The team screen (0), the Quit icon of the status and movement screens and where a move ends: closes the iris, turns the bars off, clears $6C8C and the scan flag $8189, sets the character on show to 6 (none) and shows its portrait, then (at $6DE9, also the entry for a new or old game) clears the panels in colour $68, draws screen 0 and runs the command loop.

The movement screen (2), from the green icon: bars and scan off, panels in $57. While the character is in combat (status bits 2-3) every arrow icon of screen 2 keeps only flag bit 0, so none can be chosen; otherwise every arrow with an exit (bit 0) gets bit 2 as well. Then draws screen 2 and runs the loop.

Handlers of the movement screen's arrows, given in turn to the location's exits by build_directions: each loads Y with the offset of its exit's second byte in the location record (4, 6, ... $12) and goes to $6E65.
Exit 2's arrow, Y = 6.
Exit 3's arrow, Y = 8.
Exit 4's arrow, Y = $0A.
Exit 5's arrow, Y = $0C.
Exit 6's arrow, Y = $0E.
Exit 7's arrow, Y = $10.
Exit 8's arrow, Y = $12.

Sends the character through the exit at offset Y. The time per unit of distance comes from agility: the average of +5 and the base at $CFB7 (an ADC with no CLC before it, so the sum can be one more), halved, then (127 - that) / 8, made odd: 15 seconds at the lowest agility, 1 at the highest, kept in $81A9. A defender, or an attacker away from the battle screen, cannot move: "YOU CANNOT MOVE IN COMBAT MODE". Otherwise the destination (+3) is the exit's first byte and the step countdown (+1) the exit's distance (bits 0-2 of its second byte) times the time per unit. A character not in combat starts moving (status 1) and the team screen comes back; a retreat stays on the battle screen.
The team screen's six character icons, in team order: each loads its number, 0 Syylk (spelt SYLK in the game's text) here, and goes to $6EEA.
Sevrina's icon, character 1.
Manto's icon, character 2.
Maul's icon, character 3.
Zark's icon, character 4.
Torik's icon, character 5.

Makes character A the one on show ($5436): points $41 at its entity record, keeps its location in $5437, prepares the arrows for it through build_directions and shows its portrait. Falls into the status screen.

The status screen (1): scan off, the five bars' lengths reset to 0 so that they grow again, panels in $29, draws screen 1, turns the bars on ($66CC) and opens the iris on the view screen if it is not open yet.

The objects screen (4), from the yellow icon: bars and scan off, both lists from their first page ($5440, $5441), panels in $73, eighty cells of the colour matrix from $0F98 set to $27. Then (at $6F62, where every object handler comes back) lists the objects here and carried, draws screen 4, and the first time round turns on the two weight bars from 0.

The objects screen's object icons are the second step of Pick-up, Drop, Ready and Activate: each records its slot in $5438 and returns. Slots 0-4 are the five carried objects in the middle column, here; $5449 holds the object in each slot.
Carried slot 1.
Carried slot 2.

Slot 7, also the first of the transporter's three destinations.
Slot 8.

Pick-up, after the object is chosen: unless it is already carried, marks it carried (flag bit 0) by the character on show (+1) and adds its weight (+2) to the character's load (+7). Pick-up is offered only when the total stays under 256 (list_objects_here); nothing compares the load with the character's strength, so an overload only drains agility. Back to the objects screen.
Drop: clears the carried flag, leaves the object in the character's location, takes its weight off the load, and if it was the object held ready (+8), the character holds nothing ready (0).
Ready for use: the object becomes the one held ready (+8), the weapon used in combat, and is picked up through $6FD9 if it was lying in the location.
Activate: runs the object's own routine, from bytes +5 and +6 of its record, through the JSR at $708A whose operand is written here, with the object's number in $5438. Back to the objects screen.
The operand of the JSR at $708A, the routine of the object being activated.
The high byte of the object's routine.

The left-hand column's page arrow: the next eight entries, of the people at beacon 1 during a transporter choice (group 5), otherwise of the objects in the location. Redraws screen 4; inside a two-step choice it counts a step ($543A) and returns so that the choice goes on.
The middle column's page arrow: the next five carried objects, or the next five people at beacon 2 during a transporter choice.
Quit on the objects and battle screens: inside a two-step choice it cancels it ($5439); otherwise back to the status screen.
Unused: clears the scan flag and goes to the status screen; no icon or jump leads here.

The battle screen (5), from the red icon: bars off, panels in $25, the location scan starts at the character's own location from the first entity. Then (at $7134, where the battle handlers come back) lists the people there, sets the scan flag $8189, draws screen 5 and runs the loop.
Handlers of the battle screen's direction icons, the second step of Attack, Retreat and Location scan: each records the offset of its exit's second byte (4, 6, ... $12) in $5446 and returns.
Location scan: the location chosen (the exit's destination, or the character's own for the centre icon's $FF) becomes the scanned location $5446 and the scan is rebuilt.
The centre icon between the arrows: chooses the character's own location ($5446 = $FF), for Attack and Location scan only (flags $29).
Unused: calls the unused $5346 and redraws screen 5; no icon or jump leads here.
The scan's eight people icons: each records its slot in $818A and returns. Nothing reads $818A, and the icons' flags stay 0, so they cannot be chosen.
People slot 1.
People slot 2.
People slot 3.
People slot 4.
People slot 5.
People slot 6.
People slot 7.
The scan's page arrow: the next eight entities, then screen 5 again; inside a two-step choice it counts the step and returns.

Attack, in the direction chosen ($5446; $FF the character's own location): with no living enemy there ($7250), "NO ENEMY TO ATTACK IN THAT DIRECTION". Otherwise the destination (+3) is that location, the step countdown the exit's distance x 4 seconds (for the own location the byte read is the one at offset $FF of the record, which matters only if the character later advances), and the status $0C, attacking.

Retreat through the exit chosen: refused with "CANNOT RUN IN THAT DIRECTION ENEMY IN THAT LOCATION" when an enemy is there; otherwise status 5 and the move at $6E65, timed by agility, staying on the battle screen.
Defend: status 8.

Returns carry set when a living entity of number 8 or more stands in location $5446; attack ($71EB) and retreat ($7225) call it. The loop runs fifty records from entity 8, so its last eight are the bytes after the entity table, $CD92-$CE21: the three unused pointers at $CD92, then the object records, read as if they were entities. The first gives status $D0 (alive) and location $80, so enemy_at always finds an enemy in location $80; as loaded, the bytes of the object records add $0C, $A2, $08 and $54.
Three bytes that decode as JMP $C200 and that nothing reaches, before the time delay unit's routine.

The time delay unit (object 17): a time lock of 120 seconds ($CF83 = $78) in which only the character who activated it ($CF84) acts, and the unit's activate flag (bit 2 of $CE0F) is cleared, so it works once. The clock's seconds' units go into $6803, which nothing reads.
The master key (object 14): opens the first door among the location's exits, of any colour ($818D = 1).

Key cards: the colour is bits 3-4 of a door's number (bits 6-7 of the exit's second byte), and each key opens the first door of its colour among the location's exits: this one colour 0 (objects 5 and 6).
Key cards of colour 8, objects 7 and 8.
Key cards of colour $10, objects 9, 10 and 11.
Key cards of colour $18, objects 12 and 13.

The door search: the first exit whose door matches (any door for the master key) has its lock at $CFC9 set to 0, open, whether or not it was locked already; the arrows are then rebuilt without redrawing the map ($6DC6). With no match, "NO DOOR TO UNLOCK".

The tool kit (object 16), for Sevrina only (character 1; anyone else gets nothing): the first door among the location's exits that is still locked is the one she starts to pick, $CF81, with status $10. With none, "NO DOOR TO UNLOCK".
Counts the bits of the exits mask of the location at ($3F) into $74.

A transporter beacon (objects 0 and 1): lists the people standing at beacon 1 (left column) and beacon 2 (middle column), blank where a beacon is being carried, and waits for one of them to be chosen (group 5) or for Quit. The one chosen, standing at one beacon, is sent to the other: destination the other beacon's location, step countdown 1 second, status 1. When it is Manto, the arrows are rebuilt for his location and the iris closes and opens again ($4A61 set meanwhile).

The transporter's ballistic control (object 2): offers its three destinations (set_transporter_icons, slots 7, 10 and 13, whose locations are at $81A6: $16, 8 and $A0) and sends the character on show there in 1 second. The search of $81A3 for the slot chosen has no end test; the slot always comes from one of the three icons.
The self-destruct card (object 15): in the location where the self-destruct unit (object 3) stands, it sets the unit's activate flag (bit 2 of $CDAD).

The self-destruct unit (object 3): arms the self-destruct ($CA06) and queues "SELF DESTRUCTION SEQUENCE INITIATED". The countdown $CA07 starts at 0, so its first second takes it to 255: the blast comes 256 seconds after arming. Activating it again does nothing.
Unused: six entries that load 0 to 5 and run into $74AD; nothing leads here.
Object 4's routine: adds one to the border colour and goes back to the objects screen. Object 4 has no activate flag, so it never runs.
Every weapon's routine (objects 18-53): takes one off the border colour. No weapon has the activate flag, so it never runs either.
